prompt.role: You are an expert healthcare data analyst extracting tuberculosis (TB) screening requirements from prior authorization (PA) policy documents.
prompt.task:
Determine whether {brand} requires a tuberculosis (TB) test as an explicit PA approval condition. Review the PA policy document below.
CRITICAL CHECK BEFORE RESPONDING: Many TB test requirements are placed in sections labeled "Other," "F. OTHER," "4. Other," a numbered universal section (e.g., "IV. Negative TB skin test..."), or "For all indications:" — NOT in the indication- specific criteria. Before outputting "NA", scan the ENTIRE document for these section labels. If you find mandatory TB test language in any such section, output "Yes" — even if the section is not labeled "Psoriasis" or "{brand}."
ALSO CHECK BEFORE RESPONDING: A vague statement about "screening for infectious disease" does NOT count as a TB requirement unless the document explicitly names tuberculosis, TB, TST, IGRA, or a TB skin test. Do NOT output "Yes" for generic infection screening language.
Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly 1 key. No explanation, no preamble, no markdown formatting.
prompt.scope:
TB testing requirements are almost always stated universally ("for all indications") or in a universal safety section. Extract the TB requirement regardless of which indication section it appears in — it applies to {brand} if stated universally.
IMPORTANT: TB test requirements commonly appear in sections that are NOT labeled for plaque psoriasis. Do NOT skip these sections:
- "## Other" with a "For all indications:" preamble (Aetna / Wellmark format) - "F. OTHER" with a "For all indications:" preamble (HMSA format) - "GENERAL COVERAGE CRITERIA: Applicable to all medication requests" (HAP format) - A numbered universal criteria (e.g., "IV. Negative TB skin test...") (Ventegra format) - Directly within the numbered PA criteria as an item (e.g., item 6: "Patient has been tested for latent tuberculosis (TB)") (BCBS/Anthem module) - "For all drugs except Otezla: [TB test requirement]"
If a TB test requirement appears in any of the above general sections, it applies to {brand} — output "Yes" even if the section is not specifically about psoriasis.

business_rules.rule:
Output "Yes" ONLY when the policy makes a documented TB test result an explicit CONDITION for PA approval. This means the patient must produce proof of a negative (or treated) TB test to receive authorization.
Explicit requirement language includes: - "Member has had a documented negative tuberculosis (TB) test" - "Patient must have tested negative for latent tuberculosis prior to initiating" - "Negative TB test required within N months of initiating therapy" - "Negative TB skin test within the previous 12 months" - "TB screening required before first dose" - "Must have documentation of TB testing" - "If positive TB test, patient has begun therapy for latent TB" - "Tested for latent tuberculosis (TB)"
These are gatekeeping conditions — the insurer can DENY the PA if the documentation is absent.

Output "NA" — NOT "Yes" — for clinical guidance or safety precautions that are NOT stated as PA approval conditions. These appear in CAUTIONS, WARNINGS, or PRECAUTIONS sections.
Clinical guidance language (use "NA"): - "Patients should be evaluated for tuberculosis prior to initiating" - "TB screening is recommended" - "Clinicians should consider TB testing" - "Use caution in patients with latent TB"
Key distinction: is a documented TB test result a REQUIRED DOCUMENT for PA approval, or is it a clinical recommendation to the prescriber? Only the former is "Yes".

Output "NA" for language that only prohibits the drug in patients WITH active TB, without requiring a documented NEGATIVE test result.
Contraindication only (output "NA"): - "Contraindicated in patients with active tuberculosis" - "Do not initiate in patients with active TB"
This is a denial criterion, not a TB screening requirement for approval.
Output "NA" if TB testing is not mentioned at all in the document.

"No" is rarely applicable. Use "No" only if the policy explicitly states that TB testing is NOT required. In practice, policies either require TB testing (Yes) or do not mention it / give only clinical guidance (NA).

The section where TB appears determines the answer — not just the word "tuberculosis" appearing in the document.
TB test = "Yes" when the requirement appears in ANY of these sections: - Numbered initial approval criteria (e.g., "3. Member must have a negative TB test...") - A universal/general section explicitly part of the PA decision: "For all indications:", "F. OTHER", "4. Other", "## Other", "GENERAL COVERAGE CRITERIA", "Applicable to all medication requests", "General requirements", a numbered universal criterion (e.g., "IV.") - Continuation/reauthorization criteria
CRITICAL: Sections labeled "Other," "F. OTHER," or "4. Other" are FORMAL PA POLICY SECTIONS — not cautions, not boilerplate. When they contain language like "Member has had a documented negative tuberculosis (TB) test," that is a mandatory PA approval condition → output "Yes."
TB test = "NA" when the TB mention appears ONLY in: - "CAUTIONS" or "WARNINGS" sections - Clinical background or disease overview paragraphs - Prescribing information references - Statements like "should be evaluated" or "monitor for" without making it a required PA condition
CONDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: A TB test stated as conditional is still "Yes". Examples that are "Yes": - "for persons who are naïve to biologic drugs" — still a PA condition - "within 6 months of initiating therapy" — still required - "unless previously screened" — still required as a default The question is: can the insurer require TB test documentation before approving the drug? If yes → "Yes".

A general statement about screening for "immunologic and infectious disease" or "infections" does NOT constitute a TB test requirement unless it explicitly names tuberculosis, TB, TST, IGRA, or a TB skin test.
Examples that are NOT a TB test requirement (output "NA"): - "Members should be screened for immunologic and infectious disease prior to initiating therapy" - "Evaluate for infections prior to initiating therapy" - "Screen for infections and immunization status" - "Standard infection screening is required"
The document MUST explicitly name tuberculosis or a specific TB test type (TST, IGRA, TB skin test, interferon-gamma release assay) before you can output "Yes." Vague "infectious disease" language → "NA."

example.policy_excerpt: 4. Other (applies to all indications): Member has had a documented negative tuberculosis (TB) test (tuberculosis skin test [TST] or interferon-release assay [IGRA]) within 12 months of initiating therapy for persons naive to biologic drugs.

example.description: Clinical guidance in Cautions section — NA
example.policy_excerpt: CAUTIONS: 1. Patients should be evaluated for tuberculosis (TB) prior to initiating guselkumab. Guselkumab should not be initiated in a patient with active TB.
TB Screening: Patient has been tested for latent tuberculosis (TB). If positive, the patient has begun therapy for latent TB prior to initiating.
[Policy document contains no mention of tuberculosis, TB, TST, or IGRA]

example.description: 'F. OTHER' or 'Other' universal section with explicit TB — Yes
example.reasoning: The section is labeled "F. OTHER" or "Other" but it is a formal PA policy section — NOT a cautions section. The language "Member has had a documented negative tuberculosis (TB) test" is a mandatory affirmative requirement. "For all indications" covers plaque psoriasis. Output "Yes."
example.policy_excerpt:
F. OTHER
For all indications: Member has had a documented negative tuberculosis (TB) test (which can include a tuberculosis skin test [TST], an interferon-release assay [IGRA]) within 6 months of initiating therapy for persons who are naïve to biologic drugs or targeted synthetic drugs associated with an increased risk of TB.
For all indications: Member cannot use the requested medication concomitantly with any other biologic drug or targeted synthetic drug for the same indication.

example.description: Vague 'infectious disease' screening — NOT a TB requirement
example.reasoning: The document says "screened for immunologic and infectious disease" — this is boilerplate prescribing information language. It does NOT name tuberculosis, TB, TST, or IGRA. It uses "should" (recommendation), not mandatory language. No specific TB test is required. Output "NA."
example.policy_excerpt:
Overview: Members should be screened for immunologic and infectious disease prior to initiating therapy.
Criteria for Initial Approval (Psoriasis): Documentation of moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis with an inadequate response to at least two of the following: Enbrel, Humira, Otezla, Skyrizi.

prompt.output_format:
Return ONLY a valid JSON object. No explanation. No markdown. No extra text. Exactly this 1 key:
{ "tb_test": "..." }
Valid values: "Yes", "No", "NA"
Return ONLY a valid JSON object. Do NOT wrap your response in markdown code blocks. Do NOT use backticks. Do NOT prefix with ```json or any other text. Your entire response must start with { and end with }.
